svg.aria-label: Why a shared vCPU measures against a ceiling that moves. Two rows show the same physical core on a quiet host and on a busy one. On the quiet host almost the whole core is available to your instance and the same workload reads as eighty per cent utilisation. On the busy host neighbouring tenants take a slice, your available share shrinks, and the identical workload now reads much closer to saturation without anything in your own system having changed. The caption advises measuring steal time alongside utilisation, because otherwise the same test run on two different days disagrees and neither run explains why.
svg.text: A SHARED CORE MEASURES AGAINST A CEILING THAT MOVES
